name: Overflow Serpent
description:
The Overflow Serpent is the drainage system's great opportunist — a large colubrid averaging 1.8 meters descended from a hybrid population of escaped corn snakes, rat snakes, and indigo snakes that colonized the undercity pipe network and then, unlike most drain fauna, maintained the ability to navigate surface environments as well. They are muscular and fast, with smooth gray-green scales and a characteristic pale ventral stripe running the full body length. The eyes are full-sized and functional, though the pupils have shifted toward a more slit-like morphology suited to both bright surface light and near-dark pipe conditions. They are non-venomous, using speed and constriction, and they are the snake most likely to be encountered by general GLMZ residents because they come up.

Overflow Serpents use the drainage system as a transit network rather than a permanent home — they emerge through storm drain openings, basement vents, and compromised pipe access points to hunt in street-level environments, particularly during warm months when surface prey density is high. They are extraordinary Razor Rat hunters and are functionally responsible for regulating rat populations in several Tier 1 and Tier 2 districts more effectively than any contracted pest service. They return to the pipe network to digest, shelter from cold, and reproduce. During the major flooding events that inundate lower GLMZ districts every few years, Overflow Serpents surface en masse — a spectacle that never fails to terrify residents seeing it for the first time and annoy residents who've seen it twenty times.

Overflow Serpents have the most visible public presence of any drain fauna, and public opinion is sharply divided along tier and cultural lines. In communities with long histories in GLMZ's lower infrastructure zones, they are simply part of street life — children are taught young how to identify them, and there is a practiced etiquette of giving them space and not handling them. In gentrifying zones where new Tier 3 residents have moved in from higher areas, they are a source of recurring panic and calls to Arcturus Civil Security. Several organized community groups in the Shelf districts have explicitly opposed extermination programs, arguing that the serpents are doing pest-control work the city refuses to pay for.
diet: Razor Rats, pigeons, large rodents, Drain Eels, urban birds
notable_traits: exceptional speed relative to drain fauna
full functional vision adapted to variable light
encounters: Most visible of all drain serpents. Commonly seen crossing streets at night, emerging from drain openings, hunting in alleys and vacant lots. Flood-event mass emergences are dramatic and well-documented. Most encounters are the snake moving away rapidly. Cornered individuals bluff aggressively but bites are minor.
known_uses: Informal Razor Rat control — their value to urban pest management is widely acknowledged in Tier 1 and 2 communities. Skins are worked by the same craftspeople who work Sump Boa leather. Occasionally kept as semi-feral building companions by long-term residents who have established a loose feeding relationship with a particular individual.
story_hooks: The Overflow Serpent population in a specific district has declined sharply over six weeks. Razor Rat numbers are spiking. Something is killing the serpents inside the pipe network before they can surface.

A gentrification developer has hired an extermination contractor to clear Overflow Serpents from a target zone ahead of a Tier 3 residential build. The community has organized to stop it, and the contractor has started receiving infrastructure-access problems they can't explain.
